reviews.title: Good Entry Level Headphone
reviews.comment: A solid entry-level wireless headphone that punches above its price point. The sound is clean and balanced — true to Audio-Technica’s studio-monitor heritage — making them great for both casual listening and critical audio. Bluetooth connectivity is reliable, and the 60-hour battery life is genuinely impressive. The all-black design is understated and professional-looking. They’re not the most feature-rich option at this price, lacking active noise cancellation, but for pure sound quality and endurance, the ATH-M20xBT is hard to argue with.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
reviews.author: Susan

reviews.title: Wonderful Product
reviews.comment: This is a wonderful product for those looking not having to choose between wireless and wired. Although lower in price than other models the audio quality is upstanding and noise cancellation works incredibly well. The cord is long enough; it could be replaced by other longer in case of need. These headphones are not as portable as it might seems, the do not sit that comfy on the neck so most likely will have to be transported on a handbag or backpack always fearing to breaking them as they might me more fragile than other models. The mic is strangely placed but it works for calls on a not so noisy space.
reviews.author: Mariano

reviews.title: Still going fairly strong after 3 years
reviews.comment: Very good quality for the price overall, I’ve had these for almost three years and I still use them almost daily. Battery lasts a very very long time on a full charge, especially when you first get it. Sound is a little better when using the cord. Very comfortable and lightweight. I’ve had to replace the soft covers for the headphones because they started to flake and smell from sweat, but this was a relatively inexpensive replacement. The only flaw I’m now facing is there is a very noticeable delay in the audio when using Bluetooth, so if you’re watching a video the audio will be slightly delayed and not match the video. This obviously is not much of a problem if you’re just using these to listen to music or just use the cord to watch videos. Overall, very affordable and high quality option that I have recommended to many people.
reviews.author: Samantha

reviews.title: Long battery life, great design, very snug fit, punchy bass
reviews.comment:
I do music production and also general listening.  After using this BT headset I have to say I am very impressed by the battery life as it can hold an entire session of production (few hours, 6 or more and for numerous days) without getting a low battery notification - After couple weeks I got my first low battery so you probably dont need to have this parked on the usb charger for many times in a month.  That is the mark of a true BT studio headphone for me and reason why I'd recommend it for just that purpose.
The bass quality is actually very noticeable but not overbearing where mid and highs would be flattened out.  However it is very punchy bass without "breaking in" out of the box.  Any low-lows will be noticeable if you need to work on a bassline sequence in Ableton or an alternate program.
The charging time itself from low to full, is at least a couple of hours which is acceptable.  Quality build is very high.  Fit-wise it is very snug to the ears and buttons are on the left side, which some people may find to have a learning curve (not a high one).  Easy to press rectangle style buttons.  I haven't used it to gym or cardio with but they aren't heavy enough to where they would fall, I think the JBL TUNE 500s are made for that, because they are feather weight "light" and do a great job cancelling treadmill noise.  Im sure these would do the job fine at the gym, they aren't bulky.
They do come with a cord in case you want to use without the internal battery, so that's a neat feature.  Overall latest BT specs and long battery Im sure these would do the job for a long time, they are my go to, audio feels twice that for the price so it almost feels like a bargain but they probably sound like $150 phones. Ive had the Monster Inspirations which have a similar price tag but they are 4x as heavy and audio signature is similar but wireless and way more utility.  I highly recommend them.
reviews.author: JDA

reviews.title: Great value headphones
reviews.comment:
For the cost, you'd be hard pressed to find better sounding headphones. These are close to being studio monitors, with the convenience of wireless features.
These headphones do a good job of separating instruments in tracks and provide a better soundstage than I expected for this price. They are a touch, and I mean barely, warm. Meaning, they are mostly neutral as you would expect from a studio headphone, with the slightest bump in the lower end. Sub bass isn't really present, but I appreciate the modest punch in the low end.
Keep in mind, these are not noise cancelling headphones. I find the ear pads fit my average sized head, and smaller ears really well. The seal they create helps block out some ambient sounds on their own. When I'm doing chores around the house and pumping some tunes, I really don't hear anything but the music. I even took these out in public once to get my tires changed. I could not hear the sounds of the storefront or the shop, even as I sat writing at the bar by the shop window. I was able to lose myself in the music and my writing without any problems. I don't find there is much sound leakage as these are closed back, but I also don't listen to my music at excessive levels (~75% at most).
The one problem I have with them so far is the fact that the earcups do not swivel much, and thus cannot fold completely flat for travel. I would have also liked to see a cheap case or bag come with this product to help in transporting them. I have purchased the WS990 BT in the past which came with a leather bag that I still use when traveling. I will likely continue to use that pair for work travel, rather than the M20X.
One concern I have for the long run is their build quality. They are mostly plastic with an aluminum band for extending the earcups. Being constructed as such, they are very lightweight. On one hand, this adds to the comfort of the headphones as I forget I'm wearing them sometimes due to their featherweight and light clamping force. However, I worry that these could be broken if I decide to toss them into a backpack and take them out more often. With the light clamping force I find that I can shake them loose if I shake my head side to side rapidly. While I don't do that often, I think that anyone looking for a headphone to wear while exercising should look elsewhere, or consider finding a different ear pad that provides more grip than the provided pleather set.
For me, these will likely be relegated to around the house wear, when I don't want to be strapped to my computer desk by my R70Xs. I'm perfectly okay with that as I do really enjoy the sound these produce for the money and the comfort they provide. I think they punch above their price in the audio department and are an excellent option for someone looking for a good, reliable headphone for casual wear.
